articles.title: IRS audit revenue plunged following workforce reductions, Treasury watchdog finds
articles.excerpt: IRS audits collected $3.5 billion less in fiscal 2025 as the agency shed thousands of auditors and other agency staffers.
articles.content:
Updated on: September 1, 2026 / 4:40 PM EDT / CBS News

Revenue from IRS audits plunged 35% in fiscal 2025 as the agency shed thousands of enforcement workers, according to a new report from the Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration, an agency watchdog.

The IRS collected a total of $6.5 billion from audits in fiscal 2025, which ended Sept. 30, down from $10 billion a year earlier, TIGTA said in its Aug. 26 report.

The group said that the number of IRS employees working in auditing and collections had dropped to 17,517 as of January 2026, a decline of almost 10,000 workers from fiscal 2024. The report added that the impact of the staff reductions may "become more apparent over time." 

"These losses present a challenge to improving taxpayer service and enforcing the nation's tax laws," the tax watchdog said. "We are concerned about how staffing losses are impacting the IRS's ability to ensure that it meets department priorities."

Tax auditor exodus

The findings come after TIGTA last year found that the IRS lost one-third of its tax auditors during the first three months of the Trump administration. The employment decline was due to cost-cutting efforts by Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency, or DOGE, which sought to slash the federal workforce through a combination of layoffs and so-called deferred resignations.

The Treasury watchdog noted that because audits can take years to complete, some of the declines could be reversed as more cases are closed. 

The IRS initiated 17% more large corporate audits in fiscal 2025 than a year earlier. But audits of new business partnerships fell 30% as a major reorganization at the agency shifted employees and delayed training for some revenue agents, the report said.

The IRS also started fewer audits of wealthy taxpayers. Agency staffers opened about 43,000 examinations of individuals with income over $400,000 in fiscal 2025, down 26% from a year earlier. As of January 2026, the agency's Global High Wealth program had 27% fewer employees than before the fiscal 2025 workforce reductions.

The Treasury didn't immediately respond to requests for comment. 

Rising tax receipts

The IRS pointed to comments made by its CEO, Frank Bisignano, during congressional testimony in April, in which he said the agency is increasingly relying on technology to improve enforcement. 

"Our advanced data and analytic strategies allow us to catch instances of tax evasion that would have been undetectable just a few years ago," Bisignano said. "Along those lines, the IRS is using artificial intelligence (AI) and advanced analytics to identify high-risk areas of non-compliance and fraud with greater accuracy."

Despite the decline in audit revenue, the IRS collected more total tax revenue in fiscal 2025 than the prior year, with federal taxes paid by taxpayers rising to $5.3 trillion, up 4.2% from the prior fiscal year, according to the Treasury watchdog group.

But Sen. Elizabeth Warren, a Democrat from Massachusetts who has championed a federal wealth tax, said the data show that IRS employment cuts are a "dream come true" for high-income earners and corporations that skirt tax laws. 

"Gutting the IRS is a win for wealthy tax cheats and a loss for working people who play by the rules," she said in a statement to CBS News.

IRS funding cuts

The drop in audit revenue marks a reversal from 2024, when the IRS planned to boost tax revenue through audits of wealthy taxpayers and corporations. Under the Biden administration, the Inflation Reduction Act directed $80 billion in funding to the IRS, enabling it to hire more auditors and revenue collectors. 

In early 2024, the IRS forecast that the additional funding would help it reap hundreds of billions of dollars in additional tax revenue by pursuing overdue and unpaid taxes. However, Republican lawmakers warned that IRS auditors would target everyday Americans and cut billions in IRS funding. 

The Trump administration has proposed additional IRS funding cuts for 2027. Policy experts have warned that further shrinking the agency's budget could make it harder to collect overdue taxes and go after tax cheats. 

"The agency has fewer revenue agents, who audit the most complicated tax returns, than it has had since the 1950s, when the economy was far smaller and the tax code was far less complex," tax analysts with the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, a nonpartisan think tank, wrote in a June blog post. 

They added, "Research shows that every dollar spent on IRS tax enforcement raises multiple dollars in revenue, which means that every dollar cut from IRS enforcement loses more than a dollar of revenue and adds to the deficit."

articles.title: The IRS slashed its staff. One result? More taxes going uncollected
articles.excerpt: The IRS slashed its auditing staff last year — but the move may have backfired as tax collections from enforcement efforts plummeted, an Inspector General report shows.
articles.content:
Economy

The IRS slashed its staff. One result? More taxes going uncollected

  • Download
  • <iframe src="https://www.npr.org/player/embed/nx-s1-5954022/nx-s1-9911270" width="100%" height="290" frameborder="0" scrolling="no" title="NPR embedded audio player">
  • Transcript

A new Inspector General's report shows that as the IRS slashed its auditing ranks last year, collection of unpaid taxes fell. Karen Bleier/AFP hide caption

The IRS slashed its auditing staff last year in what was billed as a cost-cutting move, but if the effort was designed to improve the government's bottom line, it has backfired.

A new report from the Treasury Department's Inspector General for Tax Administration shows that revenue from audits plunged 35% in fiscal year 2025, meaning billions of dollars in taxes went un-collected. The drop coincides with a 27% cut in enforcement and collection staffing at the IRS, as part of Elon Musk's campaign to boost government efficiency.

"The downstream effects of these reductions are likely to become more apparent over time," the Inspector General wrote.

The IRS had beefed up its auditing ranks during the Biden administration, in an effort to collect more of the estimated $696 billion dollars in taxes that go unpaid every year, mostly as a result of people and businesses that under-report their income.

The increased staffing led to a 41% increase in audit-related revenue in 2024 — but that was largely reversed last year. More than 25,000 IRS employees were laid off or took early retirement in 2025, including about 3,600 tax examiners.

The loss in tax revenue from decreased audit activity outweighs any savings from reduced staffing at the tax-collection agency.

"Defunding the IRS is not a money-saving proposition because you have fewer employees," says Natasha Sarin, who served as a counselor on tax policy to former Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen. "It is a money-losing one, because you do a less good job of collecting taxes."

Audits generated $10 billion in tax revenue in fiscal year 2024 but that dropped to $6.5 billion in 2025.

Tax audits have been a tool to increase compliance

The Inspector General notes that the overall loss of revenue could be larger, since tax audits are primarily designed to promote voluntary tax compliance by filers wanting to avoid one.

"You're less likely to speed when you know that there's a cop on the beat," says Sarin, who's now a professor at Yale Law School.

IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank Bisignano defended the agency's tax enforcement record. Bisignano told lawmakers earlier this year the agency is using technology to target its tax audits more efficiently.

The increased staffing at the IRS under the Biden administration was aimed at bringing increased scrutiny to wealthy individuals and partnerships. That fell off sharply as thousands of auditors were let go. Audits of partnerships fell 76% between 2023 and 2025.

"Disproportionately, this is about the tip-top of the [income] distribution," Sarin says. "Something like the top 1% of earners are responsible for something like a third of the tax gap."

Staffing levels at the IRS continued to decline in the first four months of the current fiscal year. The Trump administration has called for additional cuts in agency funding in 2027.

articles.title: Clip of Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese's 'court chemistry' is getting a lot of attention from fans
articles.excerpt: Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese have been rivals for a number of years, but they will once again be working as teammates at this month's FIBA Women's Basketball
articles.content:
Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese have been rivals for a number of years, but they will once again be working as teammates at this month’s FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup.

Team USA will kick off their tournament this coming Friday with a group game against China.

They then face Italy on Sunday before clashing with the Czech Republic on Monday, September 7.

Ahead of their group campaign getting underway, TNT Sports U.S. shared an old clip of Clark and Reese playing together for the USA and mentioned their ‘court chemistry’.

They stated: “That CC and Angel Reese court chemistry. Their connection in Berlin is about to be DIFFERENT.”

That CC and Angel Reese court chemistry 😮‍💨

Their connection in Berlin is about to be DIFFERENT 🔥 pic.twitter.com/ZJbvkljfwG

— TNT Sports U.S. (@TNTSportsUS) August 31, 2026

That CC and Angel Reese court chemistry 😮‍💨

Their connection in Berlin is about to be DIFFERENT 🔥 pic.twitter.com/ZJbvkljfwG

Fans react to Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese’s ‘chemistry’

The clip has gone pretty viral and is close to reaching 5,000 likes at the time of writing.

Many fans have also commented on the post to express their opinions about the pair’s chemistry.

One fan claimed: “The chemistry is giving bestie energy and everyone noticed.”

But another suggested: “They hate each other you can tell.”

A third echoed: “They hate each other so much too.”

Another stated: “They really hate each other —- what kinda dap up was that.”

“I do find it pretty funny they are perfect teammates for each other’s game,” tweeted a fifth.

I do find it pretty funny they are perfect teammates for each others game. https://t.co/9Dwyczxpng

— BOBBYMVP👑 (@mEdia_creates) August 31, 2026

I do find it pretty funny they are perfect teammates for each others game. https://t.co/9Dwyczxpng

Another responded: “They really don’t have chemistry; if you’ve watched them on the court together you would know this.”

A seventh suggested: “When they can stop bickering for a few minutes, they actually play pretty well together.”

Still, regardless of what some fans think, it will be interesting to see how they fare together for the USA in the coming tournament.

articles.title: Yankees vs. Angels preview: Cam Schlittler's 1.14 road ERA meets Reid Detmers in pitching duel
articles.excerpt: New York Yankees take on the Los Angeles Angels as Aaron Judge nears a return and the wild card playoff race heats up. See the pitching matchup and betting picks.
articles.content:
Aaron Judge could return this week as New York looks to secure a Wild Card spot in the playoff race

Jose Caballero's pitch clock antics result in wild hot-mic moment

New York Yankees infielder Jose Caballero got into a heated discussion with a home plate umpire about his pitch clock antics on Wednesday. (This video contains AI-assisted content.)

Believe it or not, we are just a day away from the first official week of College Football. Sure, we had Week 0, and those games count, but this is the first week where everyone is back in action. That means baseball will take a bit of a backseat to football coming up very shortly. However, we would be foolish to ignore it completely as the playoff race is heating up, and on those off days for football, this is where we can make extra money. Tonight we will do that as the Yankees take on the Angels.

The New York Yankees are still in second place within their division, and to me, they still seem to be essentially the same team they've been since about June. Aaron Judge went down after the May 31 game, but is now slated to potentially be back this week or next. The team was 13 games above .500 with Judge, so they have played well even without their leader on the field. Getting him back will be a shot in the arm as they look to secure a Wild Card spot.

Cam Schlittler (31) of the New York Yankees looks on while pitching in the seventh inning during Game Three of the American League Wild Card Series between the Boston Red Sox and the New York Yankees at Yankee Stadium in New York, New York, on Oct. 2, 2025. (Daniel Shirey/MLB Photos via Getty Images)

Part of the reason for the Yankees' success is that they've had very good pitching this year. As a team, they have a 3.25 ERA and a 1.18 WHIP. One of their best pitchers goes tonight, as they have gotten a phenomenal season out of Cam Schlittler. For the year, Schlittler is 12-6 with a 2.09 ERA and a 0.97 WHIP. He also has 201 strikeouts, putting him at sixth in the Majors. He has been phenomenal on the road this season with a 1.14 ERA in his visiting starts, and that's in almost 30 more innings thrown on the road than at home. Only Josh Lowe has faced Schlittler, and he is 2-for-4 against him.

The Los Angeles Angels are a disaster once again, but there is finally some reason for optimism. The team just announced that they've been sold, which is something the fans have been calling for over the past few years. I want to defend the franchise a little bit - at least they spent money and tried. There are many franchises that are bad that never really try for free agents. Unfortunately, the ones the Angels tried for were old, uninterested in baseball, injured, or just didn't work out. Sure, they had Mike Trout and Shohei Ohtani at one point, and never won a playoff game (rarely even getting there). However, Trout was always injured, as were many other guys on the roster. Still, sometimes the best thing for a team and franchise is change.

Mike Trout #27 of the Los Angeles Angels celebrates scoring in the first inning against the Houston Astros at Angel Stadium of Anaheim on July 29, 2026 in Anaheim, California. (Photo by Joe Scarnici/Getty Images) (Joe Scarnici/Getty Images)

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

One thing they do not want to change is the production they've gotten out of today's starter Reid Detmers. This season has been great for Detmers. He is 4-8 with a 3.54 ERA and a 1.07 WHIP. His 174 strikeouts put him at 11th in baseball as well. Overall, his ERA is 25th, and his WHIP is 10th. Those aren't Cy Young numbers, but they are certainly front of the rotation numbers. He has been equally good at home as on the road, pitching slightly better at home. He did face the Yankees earlier, allowing just one earned run over seven innings on four hits.

Los Angeles Angels center fielder Mike Trout looks on against the Minnesota Twins at Target Field in Minneapolis, Minnesota, on July 11, 2026. (Brace Hemmelgarn/Minnesota Twins/Getty Images)

There are a few different ways to look at this game. I think the value is actually on the Angels as they are +141 tonight. Schlittler has been awesome on the road, but that doesn't mean he is definitely going to win the game. Detmers has also been very good. I think the better bet is to take the under 7 or 7.5. Neither starter is likely to give up a ton of runs. I will play the under and sprinkle the Angels moneyline. Vibes might be high in the clubhouse with the announcement of the sale.

articles.title: Yankees 6-3 Angels (Sep 2, 2026) Game Recap - ESPN
articles.excerpt: Expert recap and game analysis of the New York Yankees vs. Los Angeles Angels MLB game from September 2, 2026 on ESPN.
articles.content:
New York Yankees @ Los Angeles Angels

ANAHEIM, Calif. -- — Cam Schlitter gave up one run and two hits in eight superb innings, and the New York Yankees scored five two-out runs in 10th in a 6-3 victory over the Los Angeles Angels on Wednesday night.

New York loaded the bases with one out in the 10th when Jose Caballero singled, the automatic runner holding at third, and Jazz Chisholm Jr. walked against reliever Luke Murphy (0-2).

Murphy got Luis Garcia Jr. to pop out, but Austin Wells stroked a two-run single to right, Cody Bellinger hit an RBI single to center, Trent Grisham hit an RBI single to left, and Ben Rice had an RBI single to right for a 6-1 lead.

David Bednar (7-3) struck out three in a scoreless ninth for the win. Yankees reliever Michael Fulmer gave up a two-run homer to Moisés Ballesteros in the bottom of the 10th.

A marquee matchup between two of baseball’s best pitchers did not disappoint, Schlittler striking out nine and walking none and Angels left-hander Reid Detmers allowing one run and six hits in seven innings, striking out eight and walking none.

Schlittler, who has an AL-best 2.04 ERA, retired 20 of the first 21 batters he faced, his only blemish a soft single to left by Vaughn Grissom in the second.

But he grooved a 95-mph cutter to Grissom in the seventh, and the Angels first baseman drove it over the center-field wall for a solo homer and a 1-1 tie.

It was Schlittler’s franchise-record 19th start in which he has allowed one or no runs, moving him ahead of Ron Guidry (1978), Whitey Ford (1964) and Jack Chesbro (1904), who had 18 each.

Detmers, who has a major league-best 1.52 ERA since the All-Star break, gave up a run in the fourth on Amed Rosario’s RBI double.

The game was delayed for about 10 minutes in the sixth when a 79.5-mph line drive off the bat of Rice hit a photographer in the head in the first-base camera well. The photographer was able to walk to a medical emergency vehicle and shake Rice’s hand before being carted away.

Up next

Yankees: LHP Max Fried (4-4, 2.80 ERA) was set to face Padres RHP Walker Buehler (8-6, 4.66 ERA) Friday night in San Diego.

Angels: RHP Ryan Johnson (3-7, 5.47 ERA) was scheduled to oppose Pirates RHP Jared Jones (2-6, 4.83 ERA) Friday night in Pittsburgh.

articles.title: Rory McIlroy's 'desire' will dictate future as Scottie Scheffler tipped to relight opponent's 'fire'
articles.excerpt: Six-time major winner Rory McIIlroy made admissions over his enthusiasm for competing at the highest level at the FedExCup; The Sky Sports Golf Podcast discussed McIlroys future and what he may need to motivate him to ge
articles.content:
Six-time major winner Rory McIIlroy made admissions over his enthusiasm for competing at the highest level at the FedExCup; The Sky Sports Golf Podcast discussed McIlroy's future and what he may need to motivate him to get back to being world No 1

Tuesday 1 September 2026 10:15, UK

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Rory McIlroy needs to assess how much he truly wants to be world No 1 again alongside balancing his home life, according to Sky Sports' Robert Lee.

The Northern Irishman finished in a seven-way tie for fourth at the FedExCup over the weekend, finishing five shots off tournament winner Scottie Scheffler despite showing earlier signs of promise.

Now 37, six-time major winner McIlroy admitted his "fuse was shorter than it used to be" before the final round at the East Lake Golf Club.

  • Scottie Scheffler celebrates FedExCup victory
  • Tiger Woods praises Scheffler for East Lake win
  • Tour Championship: Final leaderboard [external]
  • Get Sky Sports or stream golf with no contract

He had arrived in Atlanta off the back of three weeks of competing in a row, something he admitted he would never exceed again despite still managing a fourth-place finish over the weekend.

"That just tells you how good he is," Lee told the Sky Sports Golf Podcast. "But I think Rory's body language this week wasn't great. He looked slightly… is grumpy the right word?

"But he's just slightly off that kind of affable, bouncy Rory that we normally see. So there's stuff going on with him… Rory's in this position. He's played golf for 20 years at the highest level. He's 37.

Subscribe now on: Apple Podcasts | Spotify | Spreaker

"He realises there are other things in life, but the last thing he wants to do is not be able to be peak Rory. So his conundrum is 'how much can I pare back my schedule, but still perform the way I know I can?' That's the place he's in now.

"37 is still golfing prime. It's going to come down, for him, to desire. How much does he still want it? And if he still wants it, I think he's going to have to play a bit more."

McIlroy took an extended break after The Open, spending more time with his family before returning for this three-week run of events.

"I absolutely think he can win more majors," Lee continued. "But going along with that is you sacrifice your home life. You're not as home as much as you want to be… I actually think Rory is in mentally quite a good place at the moment, and he is focused on some family stuff at the moment."

Speaking before his final round, McIlroy admitted: "once you lose your enthusiasm to go to the course, it is time to take a break." That comment could suggest golf fans could be seeing less and less of the world No 2 as time goes on.

"I think that's plausible," Sean Zak, writer for Golf.com, agreed. "I think that the changes coming to the PGA Tour schedule could pull a little bit more out of him, could help him balance being a dual member a little bit better."

Zak went on to suggest McIlroy may need to set himself a goal of beating Scheffler to top spot to reignite his motivation.

"You know, of all the golfers at the top of the game, I think he better than most shows what things matter to him and shows the goals that he's set," he said.

"And I think ever since that Grand Slam-finishing Masters win, he has just struggled to really place "OK, what's the next goal?"

"When you look at 2025, when he won that Masters, the next goal was really, 'OK, let's win at Bethpage' - and then they did that.

"Then after that, it was 'gosh, OK, what is the next goal?' I think for him to live up to what we're asking him to do right now, what a lot of fans would like him to do, is his next goal needs to be taking Scottie off the top mark or matching Scottie in some way.

"I bet if Scottie won a major this year, Rory might feel a little bit more of the fire beneath him because you get to some point where they've all won a bunch.

"What is the tiebreaker? How many majors did you win? Rory still has a nice little lead on Scottie - but how long will that last? We think that he probably won't hold that lead.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"It's just funny because I think Rory McIlroy, let's say [at] 21 years old was like "I want to be number one in the world. I want to win every single tournament."

"Rory McIlroy, 37-year-old, he may have to do the same thing. It should be 'I want to be number one. I want the world to think I'm the best golfer because at my best, I certainly am.'"

What's next?

McIlroy will take a week off before returning to defend his Amgen Irish Open title, held at Trump International Golf Links in Doonbeg from September 10-13, a year on from his dramatic play-off win at The K Club.

articles.title: Rory McIlroy admits he's not interested in playing most PGA Tour events moving forward
articles.excerpt: Rory McIlroy says his PGA Tour schedule will keep shrinking, admitting after the Tour Championship that his enthusiasm for playing every week has decreased.
articles.content:
The six-time major champion spoke candidly about his shrinking schedule after his third round at the Tour Championship

LIV Golf Collapse Is Here And The PGA Tour Has A BIG Problem | Don't @ Me w/ Dan Dakich

LIV golf is all but finished, but a dark cloud now hangs over the players: what happens next? Dan Dakich and crew discuss how the PGA will respond.

Golf is often seen as a very staid, traditional sport where little changes over time. But the past few years have been a tumultuous period in the professional game, at least, with the rise and now seeming fall of the LIV Golf Tour.

LIV's impact hasn't just been limited to their events, players and debate over how their tournaments should be weighed for major qualification or evaluated for Ryder Cup team selection. The PGA Tour, in response to LIV's formation, was essentially forced to make changes to keep top players in place.

Signature events with higher purses. Changing some tournaments to have no cuts. More support for the big names. All changed how the tour worked and who played in what events. The signature events enjoyed better competition as star players competed for $20 million in prize money, but some smaller tournaments suffered as golfers chose rest rather than travel and play for smaller rewards.

PGA TOUR ANNOUNCES SWEEPING CHANGES TO SCHEDULE: EVERYTHING YOU NEED TO KNOW ABOUT NEW TWO-TIERED SYSTEM

Rory McIlroy competes on day three of the 2025 BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth Golf Club in Virginia Water, Surrey, England, on Saturday, Sept. 13, 2025. (Adam Davy/PA via AP)

One of the key personalities in these changes and negotiations on the PGA Tour has been Rory McIlroy. McIlroy committed to the PGA Tour when others were bolting, assumed a leadership role with commissioner Jay Monahan on the PGA's response and has become increasingly vocal as he becomes a "veteran" at 37-years-old.

And with the tour facing an even more aggressive set of changes under new CEO Brian Rolapp, McIlroy spoke about what that might mean for his schedule. Which seems to be decreasing each season.

After his third round at the Tour Championship in Atlanta, McIlroy admitted that his interest in playing most tournaments has decreased as he progresses through his career.

"I think once you lose your enthusiasm to go to the course, it is time to take a break," McIlroy said.

"I've turned up to events that I haven't necessarily wanted to be there because I feel like I should be there."

RORY MCILROY GETS SNARKY ON THE RETURN OF LIV GOLF PLAYERS TO PGA TOUR: 'HAVE THEY BROUGHT VALUE?'

Rory McIlroy reacts on the second hole during the first round of the Tour Championship golf tournament Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026, in Atlanta. (AP Photo/Colin Hubbard)

McIlroy took a break after The Open Championship before returning to play three straight weeks in the FedEx Cup Playoffs. He told reporters that's his limit these days, as he looks to spend more time with his family and take more breaks from competition.

"This is my third week in a row. I rarely do that anymore, and I feel like that is my limit," he said.

"If I had to tee up again next week, that to me is tough."

He also said he'll never play four straight weeks in a row moving forward, and that his "fuse" has gotten shorter over time.

"But again, I am 37. This is my 18th or 19th year as a professional, so my fuse is a little shorter than it used to be," he added.

As for the reduced schedule he wants to play, McIlroy said it's likely going to get even smaller, "I play my schedule and I'll continue to play my schedule, which is getting less and less as the years go on."

Regarding the changes made to the PGA Tour moving forward, two different "tracks" for events, as well as promotion and relegation for the first time ever, he doesn't seem too excited for what that might mean. And blames LIV, in some small part, for what's happened.

"It's funny. Like I think, as they've done all this work, you start to realize that the way the tour was before LIV came along was actually pretty good," he said. "It was a pretty good structure, and everything sort of worked pretty well. LIV created this false economy where we had to up prize funds and had to cut fields and try to support the top players and all that stuff, which I think needed to happen because that was the only way to retain talent at the time.

"But now that LIV looks like it's less of a threat, I think the old ways of the PGA Tour weren't actually that bad."

Rory McIlroy reacts on the second green during the first round of the Tour Championship golf tournament Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026, in Atlanta. (AP Photo/Colin Hubbard)

Part of that increasing willingness to be honest about his views on golf, his place in the tour, and the future, is that McIlroy in some ways felt abandoned by Monahan, that all his efforts to keep the PGA Tour together weren't appreciated. Now, with rumors suggesting that some LIV players, including two-time major champion Jon Rahm, might be looking to return, it seems he's feeling further and further removed from the weekly grind of a PGA Tour schedule.

OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

Major championships are the priority, with the FedEx Cup Playoffs a distant fifth. Oh, and TGL somewhere in there, too.

McIlroy's earned the right to do what he wants. At the same time, though, he's one of the sport's biggest draws. With the tour hoping to bring in even more high-dollar sponsors, it might be a tougher sell when McIlroy is this open about playing fewer tournaments. Even with big purses. Seems like he feels that's their problem to figure out.

Ian Miller is a writer at OutKick.

articles.content:
• Rumor Roundup

Big change planned for Ivy Nile, status of UpUpDownDown, Stephanie Vaquer breakup, Andre’s giant fart, and more rumors!

Now that The Creed Brothers are back in NXT, what does Ivy Nile’s future look like in WWE? Let’s see what today’s rumors have to say about it!

Top rumor of the day: Big change for Ivy Nile

According to Fightful Select, Ivy Nile’s WWE contract is set to expire this fall.

Even though Ivy has been relegated to mostly working on WWE’s C-show Main Event this year, it sounds like WWE has a “big change” planned for her if she does indeed re-sign with the company. That comes from sources in WWE Creative, who also claim that these plans for Nile have been under development “for quite a while.”

If it’s true that WWE has recently been discussing creative plans for Ivy Nile, there’s reason to be optimistic about the two sides working out a deal for her to remain with the promotion. Then again, all it takes is an insulting 50% pay cut offer for any negotiation to go south.

The rest of the rumors!

  • Don’t get your hopes up about the return of UpUpDownDown now that The New Level and Austin Creed (fka Xavier Woods) are in AEW. That’s because former WWE star Tyler Breeze confirmed on X that WWE owns that intellectual property.
  • There is a lot of speculation that WWE superstar Stephanie Vaquer and NXT wrestler Myles Borne may have broken up after they unfollowed each other on social media and deleted various comments and pictures of themselves together.
  • For whatever it’s worth, Andrade told Luchando Por Tus Sueños that he’s currently making more money in AEW than he was being paid in WWE.
  • After Nick Hogan recently told TV Insider that his relationship with his sister Brooke is “in a really good place” right now, Hulk’s daughter clarified to Us Weekly that she and Nick are “not in communication, and his characterization of our relationship does not reflect my experience.”
  • During an interview with 12 News, Jake “The Snake” Roberts said Andre the Giant once got him down in the corner of the ring and laughed while he “sat on me and farted for a good 30, 40 seconds. It was the most amazingly long fart in all mankind. I didn’t think it was ever gonna stop…It was horrible.”
